explain.say: Imagine two tall pea plants in a garden. You plant their seeds, and some of the babies come up short! How can tall parents have short children? Let's follow the genes step by step.

explain.say: Now see this 2 by 2 grid, called a Punnett square. Two choices from mum times two from dad makes 4 boxes, 4 equally likely ways for the gametes to meet. Can you count the boxes?
Fill the boxes and you get 1 TT, 2 Tt and 1 tt. Big T is dominant, which means it shows whenever it is there, so TT and Tt are both tall. Which plant is short?

explain.say: So 3 out of 4 pea plants are tall, and 1 out of 4 is short: the famous 3 to 1. Brilliant! Wow fact: Gregor Mendel counted 787 tall and 277 short pea plants, very close to 3 to 1.

faq.a: Tt is a genotype, the pair of alleles a plant has. Big T is the allele for tall and small t is the allele for short. A plant with one of each is called heterozygous.

faq.q: Why does each gamete get only one allele?
faq.a: Gametes are made by meiosis, which separates the two copies of each chromosome. So each pollen grain or egg cell carries just one allele of each gene, T or t.

faq.q: What is the genotype ratio from Tt x Tt?
faq.a: One TT, two Tt and one tt, a ratio of 1 to 2 to 1. There are two ways to get Tt: T from the first parent and t from the second, or the other way round.
asks: Tell me about 1 TT 2 Tt 1 tt

faq.q: Why is the ratio 3 tall to 1 short?
faq.a: T is dominant, so TT and Tt plants are both tall. Only tt plants, with no T at all, are short. That gives 3 tall for every 1 short.

faq.q: Does 3 to 1 mean exactly 3 tall in every 4 seeds?
faq.a: No. It is a probability. With 4 seeds you might get 2 short or none. With hundreds of seeds, the numbers get closer to 3 to 1.
asks: Is a Punnett square a promise?

facts: Mendel reported 787 tall and 277 dwarf pea plants from crossing hybrids, a ratio of about 2.84 to 1.
A cross between two heterozygous parents gives a 1:2:1 genotype ratio and a 3:1 phenotype ratio.
